- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ levels), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model underestimates the true mean of the 30-day price range, particularly in the latter half of the forecast.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the first 10–15 days, then drifts downward — suggests lag in adjusting to downward momentum.
- Model fails to account for strong downward momentum in the final 5–10 days of the history, leading to underestimation of true price decline.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility (e.g., spikes in 70s–80s) by forecasting higher prices than true outcome, then fails to adjust for subsequent correction.
- Model underestimates the true “bottom” of the price range, especially in the final 5–10 days, suggesting it doesn’t recognize price exhaustion or mean reversion.
- Model tends to smooth out sharp declines, underestimating the true magnitude of downward movement.
- Model overestimates the “recovery” phase after a dip — fails to recognize that prices often return to prior levels without full rebound.
- Model exhibits “anchoring” bias — overweights recent high prices and underweights recent low prices in forecasting.
